newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise report adds confidence - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise report adds confidence - analysts.

text.p: News of a successful well appraisal at the Cerro Falcone area has given industry watchers extra confidence that Enterprise Oil Plc is making good progress in developing its promising Italian operations.
But the drilling success was not so big as to signify a major breakthrough for the British firm in the southern Appenines, analysts said.

Enterprise earlier on Wednesday said it had completed appraisal of the Cerro Falcone-2 well after drilling a second, sucessful horizontal arm by partner and operator Agip SpA, which has a 45 percent interest.
"It's a question of adding confidence more than anything else," said Gordon Gray at Salomon Brothers.

The second arm, which will see the start of a long-term test in mid-1997, proved more succesful than the first. That branch was already tested in October after a main vertical well was drilled in April 1996.
It is the first time the bilateral well method has been used in Italy. But because of technological problems, the process cannot be fully exploited in Cerro Falcone-2, Enterprise said.
Different characteristics of the two arms do not allow their production to be mixed together, which would have allowed two taps into the same reservoir without having to drill a separate well.

"You would effectively get two wellbores for the price of one and a bit," Simon Oddie, Enterprise's general manager in Rome, told Reuters in a telephone interview. "(But) we couldn't really do that in this instance because the performance of the second lateral section would probably not have allowed the first section to flow very much."
The first horizontal branch was tested at 1,200 barrels of light oil per day, while the second arm tested 6,604 barrels.
The bilateral technology will now be used in future drilling operations in the entire Val d'Agri area, Oddi added.
A rig is currently being moved down from Northern Italy to Cerro Falcone-1, the original discovery well, to drill a single lateral off the vertical well.
At the same time, the rig on Cerro Falcone-2 will be moving to Volturino-1, which is on the same production concession, to test an extension of another accumulation.
The rig will then come back to drill Cerro Falcone-3. The Cerro Falcone-3 study is scheduled to start about nine months from now, Oddie said.
Shares in Enterprise rose 12 pence to 653-1/2 by 1451 GMT. -- Hans de Jongh, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
